description: Use this skill for any feature work, bug fix, refactor or scaffolding in a Go backend that uses, or should use, a command/query/event architecture (CQRS, event-driven, DDD, hexagonal), even when none of those terms appear. Trigger on: adding or changing a use case or endpoint that writes or reads business state; enforcing a business rule; needing other parts of the system to be notified or to react when something happens (domain events, policies, cross-context or cross-service reactions); separating reads from writes or decoupling side effects from a handler; fixing HTTP status codes or error logging in handlers; bootstrapping a new Go microservice or bounded context; or working in code that imports internal/platform/cqrs, buses, aggregates or unit of work. Also use it to review Go code for CQRS/EDA violations. Skip generic Go tasks (logging, benchmarks, plain Kafka consumers), non-Go code, and conceptual-only questions.

results.query: we're spinning up a new go microservice for subscription billing — plans, subscribe, cancel, renew. set up the repo structure, I want it event driven so other services can react to subscription changes
in services/orders (go) add an endpoint to refund an order. refunds for orders older than 30 days aren't allowed, and accounting needs to know whenever a refund happens
can you review internal/inventory? my teammate added a ReserveStock handler that also decrements the warehouse aggregate and sends an email directly, something smells off but I can't say what
add a use case to approve a loan application in our Go service. The approval rules already live in the LoanApplication aggregate, just wire it up through the command bus and expose it over http
GET /customers/{id}/balance returns 500 for unknown customers and every 409 shows up as ERROR in our logs. can you fix both? it's the go service that uses internal/platform/cqrs

refactor this go handler: it validates the request, updates postgres in a transaction, publishes to our event bus and returns the updated user. I'd like writes and reads separated properly and the side effects decoupled
when a payment fails in internal/payments the related order should go back to pending. how do I wire that up in our go code? we already raise domain events from the aggregates
set up a go project for a warehouse service with a DDD / hexagonal structure, domain events and a unit of work over postgres
add 'mark shipment as delivered' to the shipping service (Go). the ordering context needs to listen for deliveries to close the order. keep it consistent with how PlaceShipment is done

our in-memory repository (go) returns the same *Order pointer to every caller and after reloading an order we sometimes see its OrderPlaced event fired a second time. why, and how should the repo look?
explain the difference between CQRS and event sourcing, ideally with a java spring boot example
my go http server leaks goroutines when clients disconnect mid request. here's the handler, how do I propagate context cancellation properly?
write a kafka consumer in go that reads json messages from the 'clicks' topic and writes them to clickhouse in batches of 1000, with graceful shutdown
set up a new go CLI tool with cobra that converts csv files to parquet, with a --schema flag
in my typescript nestjs app, how do I use @nestjs/cqrs to dispatch a command from a controller and handle it in a saga?
write table-driven go unit tests for this function that parses ISO8601 durations like P1DT2H
add structured logging with slog to this go function and include the request id from the context in every line
design a postgres schema for an event store with snapshots and optimistic concurrency on the stream version, we're going full event sourcing
build a react dashboard that shows orders per day as a bar chart, reading from our /orders API
benchmark these two go implementations of a ring buffer and tell me which allocates less
